correctness.rationale: Gamma(10,m) is minimum count of tenth-power summands needed to cover EVERY residue; zero padding allowed and gamma(10,1)=1. For p odd!=5, nonzero-base Hensel lifting is possible since p does not divide 10: for all a>=2, gamma(10,p^a)=max(g_p,z_p), where g_p covers F_p and z_p is shortest nontrivial sum of tenth-power units equal to zero. Necessity of z_p follows by representing residue p mod p^2. For p>=6000, Fermat curve X^10+Y^10=cZ^10, genus36, Hasse–Weil and <=30 coordinate-zero/projective exceptions yield at least p-29-72sqrt(p)>0 unit representations of each nonzero c. Thus g_p=2; z_p=2 for p=1 mod4 and 3 for p=3 mod4. An independent exact bitmask implementation enumerated all 781 odd primes p<6000 excluding 5, checked the 24 exceptional prime-layer rows and 18 high-power exceptions from the inspected prime_exceptions.csv with zero mismatches. For p=2, odd tenth powers are 1 mod8; gamma exponents 1,2,3=>1,3,7 and >=4=>8, with lower bound via residue 8 mod16. For p=5, tenth powers mod25 are 0,+1,-1 giving sharp12, and binomial lifting by changing a unit base by 5^(a-1) maintains 12 for all a>=2; mod5 gamma=2. CRT gives gamma(10,m)=max of local prime-power values. Full exception lists and boundaries are in inspected RESULT.md/prime_exceptions.csv; pre-existing global supremum12 is not claimed novel.
